## Purpose

Fixes #53144 — Whisper transcription silently drops audio when the decoder stops early inside a chunk.

Each audio chunk is decoded exactly once. When the model emits end-of-transcript before the chunk it was given is exhausted, everything after its last timestamp is transcribed by nobody: `HTTP 200`, a `duration` covering the whole file, `text` that reads like a finished sentence, and no field anywhere saying something is missing.

It is not the chunking — it reproduces on a file **shorter than 30 s**, where no splitting happens at all.

## Not a duplicate

At the time this PR was opened there was no open PR for this. **#53236 was opened afterwards, for the same issue, and takes the same overall approach** (re-submit the abandoned tail). The differences are substantive rather than stylistic, and I would rather they be judged than quietly ignored:

| | this PR | #53236 |
|---|---|---|
| protection against invented text | speech-density test on recovered regions | none |
| response formats fixed | all (coverage read from token ids) | `verbose_json` only |
| gap threshold | 2 s | 0.5 s — fires on ordinary trailing silence |
| slice boundary | pre-roll + seam de-duplication | cut exactly at the last timestamp, mid-word |
| bounds | pass ceiling, error handling, log line when a stretch is left unrecovered | none |

The first row is the one I would ask a reviewer to weigh. An abandoned stretch is usually **silence**, and Whisper does not stay quiet over silence — measured on this deployment, 13.8 s of near-silence came back as `" Let's go."` with `avg_logprob -0.46`, a perfectly ordinary sentence that no blocklist would carry. Re-submitting without a guard trades a silent LOSS of speech for a silent INVENTION of it, which is worse: a user notices a missing tail, but not a fluent sentence in the middle of their transcript.

I have no stake in which branch lands. If the maintainers prefer #53236, the guards here can be folded into it, and I am happy to do that work.

## Measurements

`v0.27.1`, `openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo`, real recordings (the ruled-out hypotheses are in the issue):

| recording | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 29.42 s, single chunk | text ends at **21.56 s** — 7.9 s of speech absent | ends at 28.80 s, 176 → **246** characters |
| 58.85 s, two chunks | tail of **both** windows lost — a third of the speech | 353 → **516** characters, 4 → 8 segments |
| speech + 12 s silence + speech | — | both halves present, nothing invented |

Coverage gap after the fix is ~0.6 s on all three — trailing silence, not speech.

## What the change does

After the per-chunk outputs are merged, each chunk's decoded coverage (from its own timestamp tokens) is compared against its length. A stretch the decoder walked away from is re-submitted as its own request and appended to the chunk it came from — so ordering needs no sorting: the abandoned stretch belongs at the end of its own chunk and before the next one, which is exactly where appending puts it.

Two details are deliberate:

- **Coverage is read from token ids, not logprobs.** `logprobs` are requested only for `verbose_json`, so reading them would leave `json` and `text` clients unfixed — and those are precisely the clients that cannot notice the loss themselves, having no segments to measure.
- **The phantom guard is speech density, not a phrase list**, for the reason given above. It is applied **only** to recovered regions, where the fallback is no text at all — exactly what the transcript had before this change. A false positive there costs nothing that was not already lost.

Everything is bounded: a minimum gap worth asking about, a pre-roll so the slice does not start mid-word (with the resulting repetition removed at the seam), a ceiling on recovery requests, and a log line whenever a stretch is left unrecovered — a silent stop would reintroduce the same defect one level deeper. Beam search is skipped rather than half-supported.

## Test plan and results

```
# unit, the three pure helpers (values taken from the measurements above)
pytest tests/entrypoints/speech_to_text/test_recover_abandoned_audio.py

# end to end, against a running server built from this branch
POST /v1/audio/transcriptions, response_format=verbose_json
  → the three recordings in the table above; before/after numbers as shown
  → server log confirms the repair path runs:
    "Transcript repair for <id>: 1 abandoned stretch(es), 1 recovered, 0 left (pass ceiling 8)"
```

Full upstream CI has not run on this branch — `pre-run-check` gates it behind a `ready` label or 4+ merged PRs, and I have neither. I would appreciate a `/ci run` if the approach looks acceptable.

The change affects transcription output, so the output evaluation is the table above: more text on recordings that were losing it, unchanged output on recordings that were not, and no invented text on a clip whose middle is 12 s of silence.

## AI assistance disclosure

**This change was written with AI assistance (Claude).** In the interest of not overstating compliance with `AGENTS.md`: the code was authored by the assistant, and I validated it by measurement on a production deployment — the patch is running there now, and a consumer-side workaround for this same defect became a byte-for-byte no-op once the server did the work — rather than by reviewing every line myself. The defect, the measurements and the reasoning above I do understand and can defend; the line-by-line review the guidelines ask for, I cannot honestly claim. If that makes the contribution unacceptable in this form, say so and I will close it — the issue and its measurements stand on their own either way.

## Note

First contribution here — please tell me if the test layout or the approach should be different. I could not find an existing test module for this entrypoint, so the unit tests mirror the source path.

🚀

Tested this PR on sm_120 (RTX 5070 Ti), `openai/whisper-large-v3` float16, against the deterministic espeak clips from #58029 (the `verbose_json` chunk-cut word loss), side by side with stock and with the seek-based prototype from that thread. I hand-ported the diff onto `vllm-openai:v0.25.1` (context drift only; the one functional change was `seek=int(start_time)`, which 0.25.1's `TranscriptionSegment` requires). `json` word count is the reference, since `<|notimestamps|>` decoding keeps the words that timestamp mode drops.

| build | first30 (30 s, 1 chunk) | long16 (39 s) | clip_long (244 s) | clip_16min (977 s) | 16-min verbose wall |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| json reference | 62 | 82 | 491 | 1977 | — |
| stock 0.25.1 verbose | 31 | 74 | 483 | 1953 (4 cuts inside speech) | 6.1 s |
| seek-based prototype | 67 | 82 | 492 | 1919 (26 s hole after a single-timestamp ending) | 16.2 s |
| **this PR** | 68 | 83 | 492 | **1974** | **6.6 s** |

Log on the 16-minute clip: `Transcript repair ... 3 abandoned stretch(es), 3 recovered, 0 left`. Every stretch stock lost came back, the phantom filter never fired on these clips (speech throughout, so no silence regions to invent over), and the parallel chunk decode is preserved, so wall time stays within 8 % of stock. The seek-based approach on its own serialises the windows and still loses a window's tail when the decoder ends on a lone timestamp, which is precisely the abandoned-stretch case this PR targets, so the two are complementary at best and this one is the more complete fix as it stands.

Two small observations:

1. The 3 words still missing on the 16-minute clip are in the last chunks. The decoder's own timestamp says 2.32 s were abandoned at the 957.68 s cut, but the energy-based chunk is a little shorter than 30 s, so on 0.25.1's `idx * chunk_size` offsets the stretch computes to just under `UNDECODED_MIN_GAP_S = 2.0` and is skipped. main's exact `chunk_start_offsets` should make that arithmetic tighter; a threshold around 1.5 s would also catch it without touching the speech-density guard.
2. The 0.5 s pre-roll shows up as recovered segments that start before the previous segment's end (e.g. 26.42 → 25.92). Harmless for text, but consumers that assume monotonic segments should know.

Happy to re-run on sm_120 after any revision.

@Perlover  I opened the follow-up PR here: [Perlover/vllm#1](https://github.com/Perlover/vllm/pull/1), targeting fix/whisper-recover-abandoned-audio.
It adds the early-EOT/tail-recovery regression test and clamps recovered segment timestamps to keep them monotonic. The focused test suite passes: 11 tests passed. Please take a look when you have a chance.

@LinzeShi Thanks for catching this. I pushed the CJK-aware follow-up in [Perlover/vllm#1](https://github.com/Perlover/vllm/pull/1). `is_sparse_recovery` now uses alphanumeric character counts with a dedicated 0.5 characters/sec threshold for the model's no-space languages (`zh`/`ja`), while preserving whitespace-word counting for other languages. I also added regression tests for complete and sparse Chinese recoveries; the focused suite passes all 13 tests.
@Perlover the PR is up whenever you get a chance to review. Please let me know if any further changes are needed. Thanks!

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

`split()` counts a Chinese or Japanese sentence without spaces as one word, so this drops even a complete transcript from a recovered clip of four seconds or more. I'd use a language-aware count and threshold here.

@@ -0,0 +1,80 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Unit tests for recovering audio abandoned inside a chunk.
+
+The numbers in these tests are measurements taken from a running
+whisper-large-v3-turbo deployment (see the issue this change fixes), not values
+chosen to make the assertions pass: a fixture invented from memory would exercise
+a server that does not exist.
+"""
+
+import pytest
+
+from vllm.entrypoints.speech_to_text.base.serving import (
+    SPARSE_MIN_DURATION_S,
+    is_sparse_recovery,
+    last_decoded_timestamp,
+    strip_seam_overlap,
+)
+
+
+class TestLastDecodedTimestamp:
+    """Whisper states how far it got through its timestamp tokens."""
+
+    def test_reads_the_final_timestamp(self):
+        init = 50365  # any base; only the offset from it matters
+        # <|0.00|> text <|5.82|> <|5.82|> text <|21.56|>
+        tokens = (init, 1, 2, init + 291, init + 291, 3, 4, init + 1078)
+        assert last_decoded_timestamp(tokens, init) == pytest.approx(21.56)
+
+    def test_returns_none_without_timestamps(self):
+        assert last_decoded_timestamp((1, 2, 3), 50365) is None
+
+
+class TestIsSparseRecovery:
+    """A few words spread over many seconds are not speech, whatever they say."""
+
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize(
+        "text,duration",
+        [
+            (" Thank you.", 13.32),  # measured phantom over silence
+            (" Let's go.", 13.82),  # measured, and in no blocklist anywhere
+        ],
+    )
+    def test_drops_measured_phantoms(self, text, duration):
+        assert is_sparse_recovery(text, duration) is True
+
+    def test_keeps_speech_at_a_real_speaking_rate(self):
+        speech = (
+            "the first words I spoke in the original phonograph a little piece "
+            "of practical poetry mary had a little lamb its fleece was white as snow"
+        )
+        assert is_sparse_recovery(speech, 15.1) is False
+
+    def test_does_not_judge_a_short_region_by_density(self):
+        assert is_sparse_recovery("done", SPARSE_MIN_DURATION_S - 0.1) is False
+
+
+class TestStripSeamOverlap:
+    """The pre-roll buys context at the price of a repeated word or two."""
+
+    def test_removes_the_repetition_the_preroll_caused(self):
+        assert strip_seam_overlap("and then the kitchen", "the kitchen has a stove") == (
+            "has a stove"
+        )
+
+    def test_ignores_case_and_punctuation(self):
+        assert strip_seam_overlap("finishing up", "Finishing up, that is all") == "that is all"
+
+    def test_leaves_a_single_shared_word_alone(self):
+        # Speech shares words all the time; one match is not evidence.
+        assert strip_seam_overlap("twenty seconds", "seconds later we start") == (
+            "seconds later we start"
+        )
+
+    def test_leaves_a_long_repetition_alone(self):
+        # Half a second cannot have produced five words: this is the speaker
+        # repeating himself, and the transcript keeps what he said.
+        assert strip_seam_overlap("one two three four five", "one two three four five six") == (
+            "one two three four five six"
+        )

+        """Re-asks for the audio each chunk's decoder walked away from.
+
+        A chunk is decoded once. If the model emits end-of-transcript before the
+        chunk is exhausted, everything after its last timestamp is transcribed by
+        nobody and nothing in the response says so. This walks the chunks, finds
+        those stretches, and submits each as its own request.
+
+        Recovered text is appended to the chunk it came from, so ordering needs no
+        sorting: the abandoned stretch belongs at the END of its own chunk and
+        before the next one, which is exactly where appending puts it.
+        """

inline_comments.body: `split()` counts a Chinese or Japanese sentence without spaces as one word, so this drops even a complete transcript from a recovered clip of four seconds or more. I'd use a language-aware count and threshold here.
inline_comments.diff_hunk:
@@ -80,6 +80,100 @@
 logger = init_logger(__name__)
 
 
+# --- Recovering speech the decoder abandoned inside a chunk -------------------
+#
+# Whisper emits timestamp tokens, and the last one before EOT is the model's own
+# statement of how far it got. When that falls short of the chunk it was given,
+# the rest of that audio is transcribed by nobody: the chunk was decoded once and
+# the cursor moves on. Measured on whisper-large-v3-turbo: a 29.42 s recording
+# (ONE chunk — no splitting involved) came back with text ending at 21.56 s, i.e.
+# 7.9 s of speech silently absent, with HTTP 200 and a complete-looking `duration`.
+#
+# The repair re-submits the abandoned region as its own request. It is bounded on
+# every side, because the failure it must never introduce is worse than the one it
+# fixes: a region the decoder refused to read is usually SILENCE, and Whisper does
+# not stay quiet over silence — it invents. Hence SPARSE_* below.
+
+UNDECODED_MIN_GAP_S: Final[float] = 2.0
+"""Shortest abandoned stretch worth re-asking for. Below this the gap is more
+likely a breath between segments than lost speech, and a round trip costs more
+than the words it could return."""
+
+UNDECODED_PREROLL_S: Final[float] = 0.5
+"""How far BEFORE the gap the re-submitted slice starts. Whisper's timestamps are
+quantised and routinely land mid-word, so a cut exactly at the last timestamp
+begins on half a syllable and the model guesses the rest. The words this
+necessarily repeats are removed by `strip_seam_overlap`."""
+
+UNDECODED_MAX_PASSES: Final[int] = 8
+"""Ceiling on recovery requests per transcription. A transcript is worth several
+extra passes, never an unbounded number."""
+
+SPARSE_MIN_DURATION_S: Final[float] = 4.0
+"""A recovered region shorter than this is not judged by speech density — a
+two-second gap holding one real word is ordinary."""
+
+SPARSE_MIN_WORDS_PER_S: Final[float] = 0.5
+"""Words per second below which a RECOVERED region is not speech at all.
+
+Measured, and the separation is not subtle: real speech runs at ~2.3 words/s,
+while a phantom over 13.8 s of near-silence came back as " Let's go." — 3 words,
+0.22 words/s, avg_logprob -0.46, i.e. "confident". A blocklist of known phantom
+phrases cannot be the defence here: that sentence is ordinary English and no list
+would carry it. Applied ONLY to recovered regions, where the fallback is "no
+text" — exactly what the transcript had before the repair existed — so a false
+positive costs nothing that was not already lost, while a false negative writes a
+sentence the speaker never said into the middle of their transcript."""
+
+SEAM_MAX_OVERLAP_WORDS: Final[int] = 3
+"""Longest repetition the seam de-duplicator removes. Tied to UNDECODED_PREROLL_S:
+half a second of speech is one or two words, three at a gallop. A wider window
+would delete repetitions the speaker made on purpose — and a gap IS a pause,
+which is exactly where people repeat themselves."""
+
+
+def last_decoded_timestamp(tokens: tuple, init_token: int) -> float | None:
+    """Seconds into the chunk where the decoder stopped, per its own timestamps.
+
+    Reads only token ids, so it works for every response format — `verbose_json`
+    is the only one that carries logprobs, and this must not depend on them.
+    """
+    last: int | None = None
+    for token in tokens:
+        if token >= init_token:
+            last = token
+    if last is None:
+        return None
+    return (last - init_token) * 0.02
+
+
+def is_sparse_recovery(text: str, duration_s: float) -> bool:
+    """True when a recovered region came back too thin to be speech."""
+    if duration_s < SPARSE_MIN_DURATION_S:
+        return False
+    words = len([word for word in text.strip().split() if word])

Tested this PR on sm_120 (RTX 5070 Ti), `openai/whisper-large-v3` float16, against the deterministic espeak clips from #58029 (the `verbose_json` chunk-cut word loss), side by side with stock and with the seek-based prototype from that thread. I hand-ported the diff onto `vllm-openai:v0.25.1` (context drift only; the one functional change was `seek=int(start_time)`, which 0.25.1's `TranscriptionSegment` requires). `json` word count is the reference, since `<|notimestamps|>` decoding keeps the words that timestamp mode drops.

| build | first30 (30 s, 1 chunk) | long16 (39 s) | clip_long (244 s) | clip_16min (977 s) | 16-min verbose wall |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| json reference | 62 | 82 | 491 | 1977 | — |
| stock 0.25.1 verbose | 31 | 74 | 483 | 1953 (4 cuts inside speech) | 6.1 s |
| seek-based prototype | 67 | 82 | 492 | 1919 (26 s hole after a single-timestamp ending) | 16.2 s |
| **this PR** | 68 | 83 | 492 | **1974** | **6.6 s** |

Log on the 16-minute clip: `Transcript repair ... 3 abandoned stretch(es), 3 recovered, 0 left`. Every stretch stock lost came back, the phantom filter never fired on these clips (speech throughout, so no silence regions to invent over), and the parallel chunk decode is preserved, so wall time stays within 8 % of stock. The seek-based approach on its own serialises the windows and still loses a window's tail when the decoder ends on a lone timestamp, which is precisely the abandoned-stretch case this PR targets, so the two are complementary at best and this one is the more complete fix as it stands.

Two small observations:

1. The 3 words still missing on the 16-minute clip are in the last chunks. The decoder's own timestamp says 2.32 s were abandoned at the 957.68 s cut, but the energy-based chunk is a little shorter than 30 s, so on 0.25.1's `idx * chunk_size` offsets the stretch computes to just under `UNDECODED_MIN_GAP_S = 2.0` and is skipped. main's exact `chunk_start_offsets` should make that arithmetic tighter; a threshold around 1.5 s would also catch it without touching the speech-density guard.
2. The 0.5 s pre-roll shows up as recovered segments that start before the previous segment's end (e.g. 26.42 → 25.92). Harmless for text, but consumers that assume monotonic segments should know.

Happy to re-run on sm_120 after any revision.

@Perlover  I opened the follow-up PR here: [Perlover/vllm#1](https://github.com/Perlover/vllm/pull/1), targeting fix/whisper-recover-abandoned-audio.
It adds the early-EOT/tail-recovery regression test and clamps recovered segment timestamps to keep them monotonic. The focused test suite passes: 11 tests passed. Please take a look when you have a chance.

@LinzeShi Thanks for catching this. I pushed the CJK-aware follow-up in [Perlover/vllm#1](https://github.com/Perlover/vllm/pull/1). `is_sparse_recovery` now uses alphanumeric character counts with a dedicated 0.5 characters/sec threshold for the model's no-space languages (`zh`/`ja`), while preserving whitespace-word counting for other languages. I also added regression tests for complete and sparse Chinese recoveries; the focused suite passes all 13 tests.
@Perlover the PR is up whenever you get a chance to review. Please let me know if any further changes are needed. Thanks!
